Surah al-Hashr (The Gathering) [Medinan; its verses are twenty-four]

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah﴾, meaning, exalts Him above every imperfection. The lam (in lillah) is extra (mazeedah), and the use of "what" (ma) is to give precedence to the majority (taghlib lil-akthar). ﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾ in His dominion and His creation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 59, verse 2:

﴿It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture﴾ from their homes. They are the Banu al-Nadir from among the Jews. ﴿From their homes﴾, meaning their dwellings in Medina. ﴿At the first gathering﴾ — this is their gathering to Syria, and the last of it was that Umar expelled them during his caliphate to Khaybar. ﴿You did not think﴾, O believers, ﴿that they would leave, and they thought that their fortresses would protect them﴾ from ﴿Allah﴾, meaning from His punishment. The predicate of "that" is ﴿their fortresses﴾, its subject, and the statement is complete with it. ﴿But Allah came at them﴾, meaning His command and His punishment, ﴿from where they did not expect﴾, meaning it had not occurred to them that it would come from the direction of the believers. ﴿And He cast﴾, meaning placed, ﴿terror into their hearts﴾ — with the ʿayn either sukūn or ḍamma (ruʿb, ruʿub) — meaning fear, by the killing of their chief Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf. ﴿They ruined﴾ — with tashdīd and takhfīf — from akhraba, ﴿their houses﴾, so that they might remove what they found pleasing from them, of wood and other materials.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 59, verse 3:

﴿And had it not been that Allah had decreed for them exile﴾ (qada, "decreed") ﴿the departure from their homeland﴾, ﴿He would have punished them in this world﴾ ﴿by killing and captivity, as He did with the Banu Qurayzah from among the Jews﴾.

This passage is from Tafsir al-Jalalayn, so I'll translate the Qur'anic quotations and the commentary as they stand.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 59, verse 4:

﴿That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. And whoever opposes Allah - indeed, Allah is severe in punishment⦆ opposed (khālafū) Allah and His Messenger; and whoever opposes (yushāqqi) Allah, then indeed Allah is severe in punishment for him (lahu).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 59, verse 5:

﴿Whatever palm trees you cut down, O Muslims,﴾ ﴿or left standing on their roots, it was by the permission of Allah﴾, i.e., He gave you the choice in that matter, ﴿and that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient﴾ by the permission to cut them, ﴿the Jews﴾ in their objection that cutting down fruit-bearing trees is corruption.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 59, verse 6:

﴿And whatever Allah restored (radda) to His Messenger from them — you did not press forward (awjaftum) against it with horses or camels﴾ — "aspired" (asra'tum), O Muslims; "against it" — "min" here is extra (za'ida); "horses nor camels" (rikab: camels). That is, you did not undergo any hardship in it. ﴿But Allah gives power to His messengers over whomever He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.﴾ So there is no right for you in it, and it is specific to the Prophet ﷺ and those mentioned with him in the second verse from the four categories, according to what he used to distribute: that each of them has one-fifth of the fifth, and the Prophet ﷺ has the remainder, to dispose of it as he wills. He gave from it to the Emigrants (al-Muhajirin) and three men from the Helpers (al-Ansar) because of their poverty.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 59, verse 7:

﴿Whatever Allah has restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns﴾ like al-Safra', Wadi al-Qura and Yanbu' ﴿belongs to Allah﴾, He commands regarding it whatever He wills ﴿and to the Messenger, and to the near of kin﴾, meaning the owner of ﴿the kinship﴾, the relatives of the Prophet from Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib ﴿and the orphans﴾, the children of the Muslims whose fathers have died while they are poor ﴿and the needy﴾, those in need among the Muslims ﴿and the wayfarer﴾, the one cut off on his journey from among the Muslims. That is, it is due to the Prophet ﷺ and the four categories, according to how he used to divide it: each of the four has a fifth of a fifth, and he has the remainder ﴿so that it does not become﴾. Kay here carries the meaning of lam, and an implied anna follows it ﴿a circulating commodity﴾ (dulah, meaning circulating) ﴿among the rich of you﴾. The fay' is the cause of its division in this way ﴿and whatever the Messenger gives you﴾, what he gave you of the fay' and other than it.

﴿For the poor﴾ is governed by an omitted element (muta'alliq, meaning dependent on or connected to), i.e., [marvel]: ﴿the emigrants who were driven out from their homes and their wealth, seeking bounty from Allah and His approval, and they support Allah and His Messenger. Those are the truthful﴾ in their faith.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 59, verse 9:

﴿And those who had settled the abode﴾ i.e., Al-Madinah (the city), ﴿and the faith﴾ i.e., they had become attached to it, and they are the Ansar (the Helpers) ﴿before them love those who emigrate to them, and do not find in their breasts any need﴾ of envy ﴿for what they have been given﴾ i.e., what the Prophet ﷺ gave to the Muhajirun (the Emigrants) from the wealth of Banu al-Nadir, which was specifically theirs ﴿and they prefer [them] over themselves, even though they themselves are in poverty﴾ i.e., need of what they give preference to ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul﴾ i.e., its greed for wealth.

**Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 59, verse 10:**

﴿And those who came after them﴾ after the Emigrants and the Helpers, until the Day of Resurrection, ﴿say: "Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not place in our hearts any rancor﴾ hatred.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 59, verse 11:

﴿Have you not considered﴾ (tanzur) ﴿those who practised hypocrisy, saying to their brothers among the People of the Book who disbelieved﴾ (ahl al-Kitab) ﴿—namely, the Banu al-Nadir and their brethren in disbelief—﴿If you are expelled, we will surely go out with you, and we will never obey anyone against you﴾ (fi khidlanikum, i.e. in forsaking you) ﴿ever. And if you are fought, we will surely support you﴾ (the lam here is the lam of oath, in all four instances) ﴿—the lam of preparation has been omitted from it (wa in qutiltum, hudhifat minhu al-lam al-muwatti'a)﴾.

Note on the translation: the Arabic gloss "al-lam al-muwattia" is the lam preparatory to the oath (lam al-muwatta'a, "the preparatory lam"), and is glossed in parentheses at first occurrence.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 59, verse 12:

﴿Even if they are expelled, they will not go out with them; and even if they are fought, they will not help them; and even if they help them﴾, i.e., come to aid them, ﴿they will surely turn their backs; then they will not be helped﴾. The answer of the (implied) oath has been used in place of the answer of the conditional in the five places, i.e., the Jews.
﴿Indeed, you are more fearsome﴾, meaning fear, ﴿in their breasts﴾, that is, the hypocrites', ﴿of Allah﴾, because His punishment is delayed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 59, verse 14:

﴿They will not fight you all together﴾, i.e., the Jews, gathered together, ﴿except within fortified towns or from behind walls﴾, a barrier (sur). In another reading, judur (walls). ﴿Their might among themselves is severe﴾, their war among themselves. ﴿You think them united﴾, gathered together, ﴿but their hearts are divided﴾, scattered, contrary to what you suppose.

Their example is like that of those before them, shortly before (ﷺ)... 

Translating faithfully:

Their example in abandoning faith is like that of those who were before them, shortly before, by a short time, and they were the people of Badr from among the polytheists. ﴿They tasted the evil consequence of their affair﴾, its punishment in this world, of killing and other than it. ﴿And for them is a painful punishment﴾, painful, in the Hereafter.

Their likeness, too, in listening to the hypocrites and in staying away from them, is ﴿like the likeness of Satan when he says to man, "Disbelieve." And when he disbelieves, [Satan] says, "Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ (He said this) as a lie from him and as a display (of piety).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 59, verse 17:

﴿So the outcome of both of them was﴾ i.e., the one who goes astray and the one who leads astray. It is also read with the nominative (ʿāqibatuhumā), as the subject of kāna. ﴿that they would be in the Fire, abiding therein. That is the recompense of the wrongdoers﴾, i.e., the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 59, verse 18:

﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah. And let every soul look to what it has put forward for tomorrow.﴾ (for the Day of Resurrection)

The verse is 59:19, and the passage is a short gloss from Tafsir al-Jalalayn.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 59, verse 19:

﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah⁠

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 59, verse 21:

﴿Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain﴾ and it had been given discernment like that of humans, ﴿you would have seen it humbled and split asunder﴾ cracked open ﴿from fear of God. And these are the parables﴾ mentioned here ﴿which We set forth for people that they may reflect﴾ and thereby believe.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 59, verse 22:

﴿He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾ (al-ghayb wa al-shahadah): the secret and the open.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 59, verse 23:

﴿He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, the King, the Most Holy﴾ — pure from whatever is unfitting for Him. ﴿The Source of Peace﴾ — possessing freedom from imperfections. ﴿The Giver of Faith﴾ — who affirms His messengers by creating miracles for them. ﴿The Guardian﴾ — from hayman (haymana, "to watch over"), meaning he is a watchful observer over a thing; i.e., the Witness over His servants with respect to their deeds. ﴿The Mighty﴾ — the Strong. ﴿The Compeller﴾ — He compelled His creation to what He willed. ﴿The Supreme﴾ — exalted above whatever is unfitting for Him. ﴿Glory be to Allah﴾ — He declared Himself transcendent ﴿above what they associate with Him﴾.

He is Allah, the Creator (al-Khaliq), the Originator (al-Bari'), the One who brings into existence from non-existence (al-Mun'shi' min al-'adam), the Fashioner (al-Musawwir) of forms; to Him belong the Most Beautiful Names (al-Asma' al-Husna), which are ninety-nine, as related in the hadith, and al-Husna is the feminine form of al-Ahsan (the most beautiful). ﴿He is Allah, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner. To Him belong the Most Beautiful Names. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ Its beginning has already been explained.
